<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PART&nbsp;I</font></b></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 1.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>BUSINESS.</b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="color:windowtext;font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">General</font></u></b></h5>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa Industries (&#147;Summa&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) was incorporated as
Southern California Plastics Co. in the State of California in 1942 and
subsequently reincorporated in the State of Delaware in 1998. Since 1946, Summa
has been a publicly-owned corporation whose Common Stock is registered under Section&nbsp;12(g)&nbsp;of
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;), and is
currently traded on The Nasdaq National Market under the symbol &#147;SUMX&#148;.&#160; Through its three reportable segments
described below, Summa designs and manufactures injection-molded and formed
plastic optical components for original equipment manufacturer (&#147;OEM&#148;)
customers in the lighting industry; molded plastic modular conveyor belt and
chain for the food processing industry; plastic fittings, valves, filters and
tubing for agricultural and landscape irrigation;<b><font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font></b>and
other molded and extruded plastic components for diverse industries.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The principal executive offices of the Company are located at 21250
Hawthorne Boulevard, Suite&nbsp;500, Torrance, California 90503; its telephone
number is (310) 792-7024; its facsimile number is (310) 792-7079; and its
website is www.summaindustries.com.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Strategy</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa has a strategy to maximize stockholder value by substantially
increasing the size of the enterprise, maintaining a consistent dividend policy
and opportunistically buying back stock in the public market, without unduly
leveraging the Company with debt.&#160; Growth
of the business under this strategy may be accomplished both organically and by
acquisition.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:-2.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;Operations.&#160;
Through its operating companies, Summa strives to achieve long-term
growth in sales and earnings by establishing and exceeding aggressive customer
service metrics, from continuous improvement in cost structure and working
capital utilization via lean enterprise and other management initiatives and by
continuously introducing new products and product enhancements.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:-2.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Organization.&#160; Summa operates
with a business portfolio concept whereby subsidiaries function
semi-autonomously to achieve focused business objectives.&#160; In general, these businesses have valuable
brands, unique patented products, commanding target market share, elite
processing capabilities and/or other attributes which allow them to succeed in
niche industrial and commercial markets.&#160;
Summa has a lean corporate staff, which provides planning, financial and
legal oversight, and financing; conducts the acquisition program and business
development activities; and manages the Company&#146;s investor relations, risk
management and employee benefit programs.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:-2.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;Acquisitions.&#160;
Summa is comprised entirely of acquired businesses.&#160; The Company will continue to seek
acquisitions which are compatible with its ethical culture, are reasonably
expected to be accretive to earnings per share within an acceptable time frame,
and have a proprietary advantage because of patent protection, brand
recognition, unique manufacturing processes or other comparable
characteristics.&#160; Acquisitions may be
new, semi-autonomously managed additions to the business portfolio or may be
smaller organizations or product lines to be merged into existing portfolio
businesses.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:-2.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company monitors the financial performance of its portfolio
companies and trends in the environments in which they operate to determine
whether they continue to fit with its evolving strategic vision.&#160; Based upon this assessment, the Company may
consider divestitures as part of its strategy of maximizing stockholder value.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">History of Acquisitions</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is comprised entirely of businesses acquired since
1993.&#160; Certain acquisitions, which relate
to its continuing operations, are described below:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">KVP Systems,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; </font></i></b>In July&nbsp;1993,
Summa acquired all of the outstanding capital stock of KVP Systems,&nbsp;Inc.,
a California corporation (&#147;KVP&#148;).&#160; KVP
designs, manufactures and markets injection-molded plastic conveyor belting for
the food processing industry.&#160; KVP is now
part of the Material Handling Components segment.</p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">LexaLite International Corporation.&#160; </font></i></b>In November&nbsp;1996,
Summa acquired all of the outstanding capital stock of LexaLite International
Corporation, a Delaware corporation (&#147;LexaLite&#148;), which manufactures
injection-molded plastic prismatic components for lighting fixtures.&#160; LexaLite is now part of the Optical
Components segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Calnetics Corporation.&#160; </font></i></b>In October&nbsp;1997,
Summa acquired all of the outstanding capital stock of Calnetics Corporation, a
California corporation (&#147;Calnetics&#148;).&#160;
The principal operating subsidiary of Calnetics was Agricultural
Products,&nbsp;Inc., which manufactures plastic fittings, filters, tubing and
accessories, primarily for irrigation.&#160;
Substantially all of Calnetics is now part of the Irrigation Components
segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Falcon Belting,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; </font></i></b>In May&nbsp;1998,
Summa acquired all of the outstanding capital stock of Falcon Belting,&nbsp;Inc.,
an Oklahoma corporation (&#147;Falcon&#148;), which manufactured modular plastic conveyor
belting used in food processing industries.&#160;&#160;
Falcon is now part of the Material Handling Components segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Canyon Mold.&#160;
</font></i></b>In September&nbsp;1998, Summa acquired
substantially all of the assets of Canyon Mold,&nbsp;Inc., a California
corporation (&#147;Canyon&#148;). Canyon had provided tool design and manufacturing
services almost exclusively for the Company.&#160;
Canyon is now part of the Irrigation Components segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Plastic Specialties,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; </font></i></b>In October&nbsp;2000,
Summa acquired all of the outstanding capital stock of Plastic Specialties,&nbsp;Inc.
(&#147;PSI&#148;), which manufactures formed and extruded plastic components for lighting
fixtures.&#160; PSI is now part of the Optical
Components segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Ram Belts&nbsp;&amp; Chains.&#160; </font></i></b>In December&nbsp;2000,
Summa acquired substantially all of the assets of the Ram Belts&nbsp;&amp;
Chains division (&#147;Ram&#148;) of Rainbow Industrial Products Corp., which
manufactured injection molded plastic chain and conveyor belting for the food
processing and beverage industries.&#160; Ram
is now part of the Material Handling Components segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Genesta.&#160; </font></i></b><font face="Times New Roman">In January&nbsp;2002,
Summa acquired substantially all of the assets of the Genesta Manufacturing
division (&#147;Genesta&#148;) of Pavaco Plastics,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; Genesta manufactures extruded sheet and
profiles and thermoformed components for the lighting and other
industries.&#160; Genesta is now part of the
Optical Components segment.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Pepco.&#160;
</font></i></b>In January&nbsp;2004, Summa acquired
certain assets from R.M. Wade&nbsp;&amp; Company, including the product brand &#147;Pepco&#148;
and product lines sold to commercial and agricultural irrigation markets.&#160; Pepco is now part of the Irrigation
Components segment.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="color:windowtext;font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Segments
and Products</font></u></b></h5>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company manufactures diverse plastic products in three reportable
segments as follows:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Optical Components.</font></i></b>&#160; In its Optical Components segment, Summa
designs and manufactures plastic prismatic lenses, reflectors and diffusers and
other plastic products, which are used in commercial and industrial lighting
fixtures and other applications.&#160;
Products, many of which are patented, are injection-molded using
specially compounded lighting grade polycarbonate or acrylic, extruded from
similar materials, or thermoformed from sheet extruded from similar materials.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Material Handling Components.</font></i></b><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#160; </font></i>In its Material
Handling Components segment, Summa designs and manufactures engineered plastic
components which form conveyer belts and chains and other plastic
products.&#160; The material handling
components, many of which are patented, are constructed of non-toxic,
non-corrosive plastic materials and are designed to be easily cleaned, meeting
FDA or similar requirements for food contact applications. The components do
not require lubrication and thus offer the advantage of operation free from
contaminants such as grease, oil and metal particles.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Irrigation Components. </font></i></b>&#160;&#160;In its Irrigation Components segment, Summa
designs and manufactures plastic injection-molded fittings, micro-sprinklers,
emitters, valves, filters and accessories, extruded tubing and other plastic
products for drip irrigation systems used in agriculture, commercial and
residential landscape and other applications.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Formerly, the Company also operated in a Miscellaneous Plastic
Components segment which was integrated with the Irrigation Components segment
in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2004, and in an Electrical Components segment
which was discontinued in September&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For financial information by reportable segment, including revenue,
profit or loss and total asset information, see Note 20 in the &#147;Notes to
Consolidated Financial Statements&#148; of the Company in this Annual Report on Form
10-K.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Research and Development&nbsp;</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa invests in the development of new products and manufacturing
processes.&#160; Only direct costs associated
with new tooling for products are capitalized.&#160;
All other costs, including salaries and wages of employees involved in
research and development, are expensed as incurred.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Production </font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Injection Molding.</font></i></b>&#160; Summa&#146;s principal manufacturing operation is
injection molding of plastic parts.&#160; Some
products are molded by third-party vendors.&#160;
Injection molds and tools are made by Summa and outside vendors.&#160; Products are made on molding machines, which
range from 40 to 1500 tons clamping force, using a wide variety of plastic
resins.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Extrusion.</font></i></b>&#160; Summa extrudes plastic sheet, profiles and
tubing.&#160; The Company&#146;s sheet and profile
products are primarily made of acrylic and polycarbonate, while the tubing is
extruded from polyethylene and polyvinylchloride (PVC).</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Thermoforming.&#160; </font></i></b>Summa vacuum
forms and pressure forms products from sheet which it produces and buys from
third parties.&#160; Tooling for the forming
process is produced by third-party vendors.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to injection molding, extrusion and thermoforming, Summa
performs additional production operations including laser cutting, machining
and welding of plastic parts, vacuum deposition, coating, assembly and testing.
Summa operates on a just-in-time basis with many of its customers, and
inventories are managed to support competitive service levels. Four of Summa&#146;s
manufacturing plants are ISO registered.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Marketing and Distribution</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa manufactures plastic products and components which are generally
sold to original equipment manufacturers (&#147;OEM&#146;s&#148;) who incorporate Summa&#146;s
components in their products, to businesses which incorporate the Company&#146;s
products in systems assembled for their own use or for their customers&#146; use and
to distributors and resellers who provide them to users of the products.&#160; Most sales are made directly by employees of
the Company, although Summa utilizes several independent manufacturers&#146;
representatives.&#160; Sales in the Optical
Components segment are almost exclusively to OEM&#146;s, while sales in the Material
Handling Components and Irrigation Components segments are primarily to distributors.&#160;&#160; The Company delivers its products
principally by truck through the use of independent freight carriers and, to a
lesser extent, by air and sea transport.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa&#146;s largest three customers, all of whom are customers of the
Optical Components segment, accounted for 10%, 5% and 4% of sales in fiscal
2005.&#160; Summa&#146;s largest customer in fiscal
2005 was Acuity Brands,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; The
Company has several thousand active accounts including Fortune 1,000 and large
privately held businesses.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Raw Materials</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa&#146;s principal raw material is pelletized plastic resin which is
delivered in bulk, or in large boxes, typically weighing 1,000 pounds (&#147;Gaylords&#148;).&#160; The Company is a large user of resin and does
not rely on any single vendor for more than 20% of its raw material. Every
material used is available from several vendors.&#160; Primary resins used include acrylic,
polycarbonate, polyethylene, polyvinylchloride, polypropylene, acetal and
nylon.&#160; Principal vendors include Arkema,
Bayer, Cyro, Dow, GE Plastics and Lucite, among others.&#160; The resins used by the Company are crude oil
or natural gas derivatives and are affected by the supply, demand and price
trends in the petroleum and natural gas industries.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">4</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Backlog and Seasonality</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;31, 2005, Summa had a backlog of orders, believed to be
firm, in the amount of $5,592,000, compared to a backlog of $6,682,000 on August&nbsp;31,
2004.&#160; The open order backlog is
comprised of orders for components and tooling.&#160;
Because the time between entering an order, shipping the product and
recording a sale is typically shorter than one month, backlog levels are not a
reliable indicator of future sales volume.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa&#146;s sales exhibit modest seasonality, except in its Irrigation
Components segment which sells to the extremely seasonal agricultural
market.&#160; Excluding the effects of
economic cycles, growth and acquisitions, the Company expects approximately 54%
of annual sales to occur in the second half of the fiscal year.&#160; Because a portion of overhead and operating
expense is fixed and, therefore, does not vary with sales volume, operating
profit may vary from quarter to quarter with more volatility than sales volume.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Competitive Conditions</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The markets for the products currently manufactured and sold by Summa
are characterized by extensive competition.&#160;
Numerous companies currently offer competing products nationally and
internationally, and in certain geographic areas the Company has competition
from local manufacturers.&#160; It can be
expected that other companies will introduce additional competing products in
the future.&#160; Many existing and potential
competitors have greater financial, marketing and research resources than
Summa.&#160; All of Summa&#146;s segments include
one or more dominant competitors, such as Filtrona and Lucite in the Optical
Components segment; Intralox and Rexnord in the Material Handling Components
segment; and Toro and Netafim in the Irrigation Components segment.&#160; In addition, some of Summa&#146;s largest
customers have the resources to manufacture products comparable to those
currently purchased from Summa, and some of Summa&#146;s customers also compete with
the Company in certain areas.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa believes that its trade names and reputation are significant to
its competitive position.&#160; In addition,
Summa believes that price is a significant element of competition.&#160; However, factors such as engineering,
performance, availability and reliability are considered in the purchasing
process.&#160; The performance of Summa in the
future will depend on its ability to develop and market new products that will
gain customer acceptance and loyalty, as well as its ability to adapt its
product offerings and control its costs to meet changing pricing considerations
and other market factors.&#160; The Company&#146;s
operating performance would be adversely affected if it were to incur delays in
developing new products or if such products did not gain market
acceptance.&#160; There can be no assurance
that existing or future products will be sufficiently successful to enable Summa
to effectively compete in its markets or, should new product offerings meet
with significant customer acceptance, that one or more current or future
competitors will not introduce products that render the Company&#146;s products
uncompetitive.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Patents, Trademarks and Licenses</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company owns and licenses domestic and foreign patents, which
expire on dates ranging to 2022.&nbsp; In addition, several patent applications
are currently in process.&nbsp; The extent to which patents provide a
commercial advantage or inhibit the development of competing products varies
widely.&nbsp; The expiration of certain economically significant patents,
particularly patents covering the highly successful Reflexor&#174; line of products
in the Optical Components segment, the first of which expires in 2008, will
likely result in increased competition, lower prices and decreased
profitability.&nbsp; In 2004, Summa settled patent infringement lawsuits with
two customers regarding one of the Reflexor&#174; patents and resumed manufacturing
and selling reflectors to those customers.&nbsp; Even so, Summa believes
incidents of infringement of the Reflexor&#174;-related patents and other patents
may increase as they near their respective expiration dates.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa also relies upon common law concepts of confidentiality and trade
secrets, as well as economic barriers created by its technical personnel,
including the development of proprietary manufacturing processes, investments
in tooling and the development of customer relationships, to protect its
proprietary products.&nbsp; Summa also has domestic and foreign trade name and
trademark registrations covering many of the names and logos which appear on
its products which are helpful in enabling the Company to maintain its present
competitive position.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;27, 2005, Summa had 528 employees, including six

covered by a collective bargaining agreement.&#160;
The Company considers its relationship with its employees to be good.</font></p>

the past three fiscal years, see Note 20 in the &#147;Notes to Consolidated

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Code of Conduct</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a long-standing Ethics Policy, and a Code of Conduct
which applies to all of the Company&#146;s employees and non-employee directors,
other than Article&nbsp;III (Financial Management) thereof, which applies to
the Company&#146;s principal executive officer, principal financial officer,
principal accounting officer or controller, persons performing similar
functions for the Company, and persons performing similar functions at each
subsidiary of the Company.&#160; The Ethics
Policy and the Code of Conduct are posted on the Company&#146;s website, and the
Company intends to post information regarding any amendment to or waiver of the
Code of Conduct on its website within five business days of the date of any
such amendment or waiver.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s facilities are well maintained, and well suited for its
operations. The Company believes it has adequate capacity to meet foreseeable
demand.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company owns several parcels of real property held for sale,
including 63,000 square feet of factory and office space in Fullerton,
California, which is under contract for sale to a third party; and 43,000
square feet of factory and office space in Bensenville, Illinois.&#160; In addition, the Company is attempting to
sublease a vacant 48,000 square foot facility in Rancho Cordova, California
under a lease which expires in April&nbsp;2006.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 3.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>LEGAL
PROCEEDINGS.</b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company encounters lawsuits from time to time in the ordinary
course of business and, at August&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company and/or its
affiliates were parties to several civil lawsuits. Summa does not expect that
the resolution of these lawsuits will have a material adverse impact on future
results of operations or financial position.&#160;&#160;
Certain lawsuits filed against the Company from time to time contain
claims not covered by insurance, or seek damages in excess of policy limits,
and such claims could be filed in the future.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;27, 2005, the closing price on The Nasdaq National
Market for a share of Summa Common Stock was $7.82.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="color:windowtext;font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.5in;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recent Issuances and Repurchases</font></u></b></h3>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fiscal year ended August&nbsp;31, 2005, no equity securities
of the Company were sold by the Company that were not registered under the
Securities Act of 1933, as amended (&#147;Securities Act&#148;).</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2003, the Company announced a plan to repurchase up to
$2,000,000 of its Common Stock with no time limit (the &#147;2003 Buy Back&#148;),
pursuant to which the Company purchased 9,169 shares at an average cost of
$7.96 per share.&#160; In May&nbsp;2004, the
Company repurchased all of its outstanding Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock for
its book value of $6,553,000, and 452,856 shares of its Common Stock for
$3,633,000, or $8.02 per share, in a private transaction (the &#147;Block Repurchase&#148;).&#160; The Company paid for the Block Repurchase
with $10,186,000 of subordinated debt.&#160;
Subsequently, a substantial portion of the subordinated debt was prepaid
using the Company&#146;s line of credit.&#160; In
conjunction with the Block Repurchase, the 2003 Buy Back was cancelled.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2004, the Company announced a plan to repurchase up to
$2,000,000 of its Common Stock with no time limit (the &#147;2005 Buy Back&#148;).&#160;&#160; As of August&nbsp;31, 2005, the status of
the 2005 Buy Back was as follows:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Description of Securities&nbsp;</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The authorized capital stock of Summa consists of 10,000,000 shares of
Common Stock, $.001 par value, and 5,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock, $.001
par value.&#160; As of August&nbsp;31, 2005,
3,940,041 shares of the Company&#146;s Common Stock were issued and outstanding and
no shares of Preferred Stock were issued and outstanding.&#160; The number of holders of record of Summa&#146;s
Common Stock as of August&nbsp;31, 2005 was 204.&#160; In addition, based upon the number of copies
of this Annual Report requested by intermediaries on behalf of their clients,
Summa estimates that there are approximately 1,400 additional stockholders
whose shares are held in &#147;street name&#148;, including approximately 435
stockholders who own shares through the Summa Industries 401(k) Savings and
Retirement Plan.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Common Stock</font></i></b>.&#160; Holders of Common Stock are entitled to one
vote per share on each matter submitted to a vote of the stockholders of Summa,
and there is no cumulative voting for the election of directors.&#160; Subject to preferences applicable to the
holders of outstanding Preferred Stock, each holder of Common Stock is entitled
to receive ratably such dividends, if any, as may be declared by the Board of
Directors out of funds legally available therefor.&#160; Upon the liquidation, dissolution or winding
up of Summa, holders of Common Stock are entitled to share ratably in all
assets of Summa which are legally available for distribution, after payment of
all debts and other liabilities and the liquidation preference of any
outstanding Preferred Stock.&#160; Holders of
Common Stock have no preemptive, subscription, redemption or conversion
rights.&#160; The transfer agent and registrar
for the Common Stock is U. S. Stock Transfer Corporation, 1745 Gardena Avenue,
Glendale, California 91204, www.usst.com.&#160;
Its telephone number is: &#160;(800) 835-8778.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Preferred Stock</font></i></b>.&#160; The Board of Directors is authorized, subject
to any limitations prescribed by applicable laws, rules&nbsp;and regulations,
to provide for the issuance of Preferred Stock in one or more series, to
establish from time to time the number of shares to be included in each such
series, to fix the designations, powers, preferences and rights of the shares
of each such series and any qualifications, limitations or restrictions
thereof, and to increase or decrease the number of shares of any such series
(but not below the number of shares of such series then outstanding) without
any further vote or action by the stockholders.&#160;
Although Summa has no present plan to issue Preferred Stock, the issuance
of Preferred Stock in the future could provide voting or conversion rights that
would adversely affect the voting power or other rights of the holders of
Common Stock and thereby reduce the value of the Common Stock.&#160; In addition, the issuance of Preferred Stock
may have the effect of delaying, deferring or preventing a change in control of
Summa.&#160; In particular, specific rights
granted to future holders of Preferred Stock could be used to restrict Summa&#146;s
ability to merge with or sell its assets to a third party, or otherwise delay,
discourage or prevent a change in control of Summa.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Anti-Takeover Devices</font></i></b>.&#160; In addition to the ability to issue Preferred
Stock, Summa&#146;s Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws specifically prohibit
cumulative voting and the right of stockholders to call a special meeting of
stockholders, provide for the classification of the Board of Directors into
three classes with one class elected annually, require a two-thirds
supermajority stockholder vote to amend certain provisions of the Certificate
of Incorporation and Bylaws, and include other provisions which are also likely
to delay, discourage or prevent a change in control of Summa not approved by
the Board of Directors and the Company&#146;s stockholders.&#160; Further, neither the Company&#146;s Certificate of
Incorporation and Bylaws, nor Delaware law, prohibit the Company from adopting
a stockholders&#146; rights plan, or poison pill.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Shares Issuable Upon Exercise of
Options&nbsp;</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of August&nbsp;31, 2005, 1,575,325 shares of Summa Common Stock were
issuable upon exercise of options granted and/or available to be granted under
its stock option plans and in connection with acquisitions, all of which are
registered under the Securities Act.&#160;
During 2005, the Board of Directors acted to accelerate the vesting of
most of the then outstanding stock options, all of which contained exercise
prices greater than the market trading price at that time.&#160; All options vest in full immediately prior to
a change of control of the Company, as defined in the stock option plans.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Dividend Policy</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Following the 2004
fiscal year end, the Company declared an annual dividend of $.06 per share of
common stock, its first cash dividend since 1983.&#160; The Board of Directors recently adopted a
policy of quarterly cash dividends, with the first such quarterly dividend of $0.06
per share of common stock paid in October&nbsp;2005.&#160; Any future cash dividends or other
distributions will be determined solely by the Board of Directors and will be
based on the Company&#146;s future financial ability to declare and pay such
dividends.&nbsp; Additionally, certain lending agreements restrict the Company
from declaring or paying dividends beyond set limits.&nbsp; In any fiscal year,
the Company may declare or pay any dividend or distribution and may redeem,
retire, repurchase or otherwise acquire shares of Common Stock in a maximum
aggregate of the lesser of $2,000,000 or the consolidated net profit after
taxes of Summa for such fiscal year.&nbsp; Transactions that would exceed these
limits would require prior bank authorization and the appropriate waivers.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additional information required by this item is incorporated by
reference from Part&nbsp;III, Item 12 of this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>

  <td width="662" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:6.9in;">
  <p style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">MANAGEMENT&#146;S
  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.</font></b></p>
  </td>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">General</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Statements contained in this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K, which are
not purely historical, are forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section&nbsp;27A
of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section&nbsp;21E of the Securities Exchange
Act of 1934, including but not limited to statements regarding Summa&#146;s
expectations, hopes, beliefs, intentions or strategies regarding the future,
such as those set forth in &#147;Legal Proceedings&#148; above.&#160; Actual results could differ materially from
those projected in any forward-looking statements as a result of a number of
factors, including those detailed in &#147;Risk Factors&#148; below and elsewhere in this
Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K.&#160; The
forward-looking statements are made as of the date hereof, and the Company
assumes no obligation to update the forward-looking statements, or to update
the reasons why actual results could differ materially from those projected in
the forward-looking statements.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa manufactures plastic products for diverse commercial and
industrial markets. Through its three reportable segments, Summa designs and
manufactures injection-molded and formed plastic optical components for OEM
customers in the lighting industry; modular plastic conveyor belt and chain for
the food processing industry; engineered plastic fittings, valves, filters and
tubing for agricultural and landscape irrigation; and other molded and extruded
plastic components for diverse industries.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Significant events and developments in fiscal 2005 included:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>During
fiscal 2005, plastic resin, the principal raw material of the Company,
experienced extreme price inflation and volatility, and the Company has so far
been unable to increase the prices of its products to fully offset the cost
increases, especially in the Optical Components segment.&#160; The resin price volatility was exacerbated
after the end of fiscal 2005 as a result of hurricane-related interruptions at
oil processing and petrochemical facilities in the Gulf of Mexico region.&#160; Further resin price increases have been
announced and are anticipated in the near future, and passing these on will
represent a continuing challenge.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman">Earnings for
fiscal 2005 were substantially lower than in fiscal 2004. Improvement in
financial performance of the Material Handling Components and Irrigation
Components segments was eclipsed by deterioration in the Optical Components segment.&#160; The Optical Components segment has initiated
a three-point program of structural cost reduction, renewed customer focus, and
an increased investment in product development activity.&#160; The Company currently expects that the first
half of fiscal 2006 will compare unfavorably to prior year results for this
segment, but year over year improvement in the second half of fiscal year 2006
is expected.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>As
previously announced, the former Electrical Components segment was discontinued
in September&nbsp;2005 when Summa sold certain current assets of its
subsidiary, Plastron Industries,&nbsp;Inc., at their book value and agreed to
lease certain retained fixed assets of Plastron to the buyer.&#160; Summa does not expect to report a material
gain or loss as a result of the transaction.<b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160; </font></i></b>Additional assets of
Plastron, principally real estate located in Illinois, will be liquidated as
soon as practical.&#160; In the past year,
significant losses were incurred by this former segment. This transaction is
expected to eliminate negative operating cash flow and permit reinvestment of
proceeds of the sale and cash flow from leases in businesses with better
margins and growth prospects.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Certain
relocation and consolidation programs in the Material Handling Components and
Irrigation Components segments were successfully completed during fiscal 2005,
and the expected operating cost benefits began to be realized in the second
half of the year.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>In
September&nbsp;2005, the Company announced a plan to pay quarterly cash
dividends.&#160; The first such dividend of
$.06 per share of common stock was paid in October&nbsp;2005.&#160; Assuming the quarterly dividends continue to
be paid at the same rate, the program will use approximately $1 million per
year.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>During
fiscal 2005, the Company repurchased 62,481 shares of its common stock, at an
average cost of $8.32 per share, in open market transactions, pursuant to a
plan to acquire up to $2,000,000 of common stock with no time limit.</p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fiscal 2005 versus Fiscal 2004</font></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sales for the fiscal year ended August&nbsp;31, 2005 increased
$4,530,000, or 4%, primarily due to the effects of price increases
(approximately $4,200,000) and the contribution of sales from recently acquired
operations in the Irrigation Components segment (about $1,900,000), partially
offset by the loss of business to China (about $850,000). Sales decreased
$867,000, or 2%, in the Optical Components segment, primarily due to softness
in demand for high-bay, high intensity lighting products, and loss of business
to China, partially offset by price increases; increased $471,000, or 2%, in
the Material Handling Components segment, primarily due to price increases;
increased $4,926,000, or 22%, in the Irrigation Components segment, primarily
due to the inclusion of sales from recently acquired operations (approximately
$1,900,000), the effects of price increases (approximately $2,200,000),
recaptured market share from certain major customers and improved market
conditions.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Gross profit for fiscal
2005 decreased $1,681,000, or 6%, from the comparable prior year period,
primarily due to increased material costs, partially offset by the effects of
higher prices.&#160; Gross margin decreased
from 25.5% to 22.9%, primarily due to increased material costs.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating expenses for
fiscal 2005 decreased $741,000, or 4%, from the comparable prior period,
primarily due to management cost reduction initiatives and the benefit of
$186,000 from partial collection of a fully reserved note receivable, partially
offset by the inclusion of operating expenses of newly acquired operations and
increased costs related to compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley rules&nbsp;and
regulations.&#160; As a percent of sales,
operating expenses decreased from 18.8% to 17.4%.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating income for
fiscal 2005 was $6,012,000, which was $940,000 or 14%, lower than in the
comparable prior year period.&#160; Operating
income decreased $3,818,000 in the Optical Components segment, due primarily to
difficulty and delays in fully passing through resin price increases and
unfavorable product mix; increased $2,153,000 in the Material Handling
Components segment, primarily due to inefficiencies related to a plant
consolidation in the prior year period, partially offset by expenses related to
a plant relocation during fiscal 2005; and increased $826,000 in the Irrigation
Components segment, primarily due to the effects of higher sales volume and
efficiencies gained from plant consolidation.&#160;
Operating margin decreased from 6.7% in fiscal 2004 to 5.5% in fiscal
2005, due to the factors discussed above.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net interest in fiscal
2005 was $71,000 higher than in fiscal 2004, due to the effects of higher
average debt levels and higher average interest rates in the most recent period
partially offset by the absence of term loan break-up fees and the write-off of
unamortized bank fees of $266,000 incurred in the prior year period.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The provision for income
taxes in fiscal 2005 was $403,000 lower than in the comparable prior year
period, primarily due to lower income before taxes.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s backlog of
unfilled orders, believed to be firm, was $6,682,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2004
and $5,592,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160;
Because the time between entering an order and shipping the product and
recording a sale is typically shorter than one month, backlog levels are not a
reliable indicator of future sales volume.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fiscal 2004 versus Fiscal 2003.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended August&nbsp;31, 2004, net sales increased by
$5,242,000, or 5%, from the prior fiscal year, primarily as a result of the
inclusion of $4,194,000 of sales from newly acquired operations.&#160; See &#147;Business &#150; History of Acquisitions&#148;,
above.&#160; Same business sales in fiscal
year 2004 increased approximately 1% from the prior year.&#160; Optical Components segment sales declined
$1,595,000, or 3%, primarily due to the loss of some contract manufacturing
work to competitors.&#160; Material Handling
Component sales increased $875,000, or 3%, primarily due to strong export sales,
sales of new products and selected price increases, partially offset by
increased competition in the domestic market.&#160;
Irrigation Components segment sales increased $5,962,000, or 36%, due to
the inclusion of $4,194,000 of sales from newly acquired operations, strength
of agricultural markets and aggressive selling efforts.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended August&nbsp;31, 2004, cost of sales increased by
$4,886,000, or 7%, from the prior fiscal year, due to the increase in sales and
increases in the cost of plastic resin. As a percent of sales, cost of goods
sold increased from 73.5% to 74.5%, primarily due to increased cost of resin
not fully passed on to customers.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended August&nbsp;31, 2004, gross profit increased
$356,000, or 1%, from the prior fiscal year.&#160;
Gross margin declined from 26.5% to 25.5%, primarily due to higher resin
costs not fully passed on to customers.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended August&nbsp;31, 2004, operating expenses were
$19,660,000, or 1% lower than in the prior year.&#160; As a percent of sales, operating expenses
decreased from 20.0% to 18.8% due to the benefit of increased sales and cost
reduction initiatives.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended August&nbsp;31, 2004, operating income increased
$519,000, or 8%, due to the changes discussed above.&#160; By segment, operating income increased
$581,000 in the Optical Components segment, primarily due to favorable product
mix; decreased $746,000 in the Material Handling Components segment, primarily
due to increased expenses related to a facility consolidation and increased
$1,111,000 in the Irrigation Components segment, primarily due to the effects
of higher sales volume.&#160; Operating margin
for the year increased from 6.5% in fiscal 2003 to 6.7% due to the changes in
gross margin and operating expenses discussed above.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For fiscal 2004, interest expense increased to $1,477,000 from
$1,400,000, due to increased debt levels as a result of the Block Repurchase
described below, and a non-recurring charge of $266,000 related to refinancing
of bank debt, substantially offset by lower average interest rates.&#160; The Company&#146;s debt and interest rates are
described more fully in &#147;Liquidity and Capital Resources &#150; Financial
Arrangements&#148; below.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For fiscal 2004, the effective tax rate increased to 36.2% from 33.1%
in fiscal 2003, primarily due to a change in the distribution of earnings among
various tax jurisdictions.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Inflation.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In fiscal 2003, resin prices were relatively stable.&#160; During fiscal 2004, especially in the fourth
quarter, prices increased so rapidly that the increases were not fully passed
on to customers.&#160; Volatility in resin
pricing resulted from high prices for oil and gas derivative feedstocks, strong
demand, especially in Asia, and reduced supply caused by several resin plant
closings.&#160; In fiscal 2005, resin prices
were less volatile after the first quarter but generally continued to
increase.&#160; This was especially true of
commodity resins, including polyethylene and polyvinyl chloride, as oil prices
increased dramatically.&#160; The Company had
difficulty passing on the full impact of resin cost increases to its customers
throughout the year.&#160; Following the end
of the fiscal year, numerous facilities which produce component materials used
in the manufacture of plastic resins were damaged or temporarily shut down as a
result of hurricanes in the Gulf of Mexico.&#160;
Prices paid by the Company for virtually all resins it uses have
increased since August&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-decoration:underline;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity
and Capital Resources&nbsp;</font></u></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Sources and Uses of Funds.</font></i></b>&#160; The Company&#146;s primary sources of funds have
been cash generated from operating activities and borrowings from third
parties.&#160; See &#147;Financing Arrangements&#148;
below.&#160;&#160; During the three fiscal years
ended August&nbsp;31, 2005, net cash provided by operating activities was
$10,248,000 in 2003, $9,711,000 in 2004 and $6,796,000 in 2005.&#160; Cash flows from operations decreased in 2004
compared to 2003, primarily due to changes in the components of working
capital.&#160; From August&nbsp;31, 2003 to August&nbsp;31,
2004, net of the effect of acquisitions, accounts receivable increased
$2,498,000; inventory increased $2,239,000; accounts payable increased
$3,786,000; and accrued liabilities increased $2,341,000.&#160; Cash flow from operations decreased in 2005
compared</p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Generally, investment in capital improvements is primarily for new
product tooling, manufacturing equipment upgrades and new computer
systems.&#160; At August&nbsp;31, 2005, Summa
was not materially committed to any outside supplier for any such capital
expenditure and believes its present capacity, augmented by anticipated
continued investment in new product tooling and equipment, will be sufficient
to meet demand for its products.&#160; During
fiscal 2004 and the first half of fiscal 2005, the Company invested in new
facilities, process improvement and automation systems, which resulted in total
capital expenditures in fiscal 2004 and fiscal 2005 which were higher than in
typical years.&#160; The Company financed
these improvements with borrowings from commercial lenders.&#160; For the three year period ended August&nbsp;31,
2005, total capital expenditures were 133% of total depreciation.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In fiscal 2005 the Company incurred long-term debt of $4,875,000
related to the new facility in the Material Handling Components segment and
debt of $1,356,000 related to manufacturing tooling and equipment.&#160; The Company paid debt of $6,340,000 including
subordinated debt of $2,309,000 and used funds of $520,000 to purchase common
stock and $240,000 for payment of cash dividends.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2003, the Company announced a plan to repurchase up to
$2,000,000 of its Common Stock with no time limit (the &#147;2003 Buy Back&#148;).&#160; Prior to May&nbsp;2004, the Company had
purchased 9,169 shares at an average cost of $7.96 per share.&#160; In May&nbsp;2004, the Company repurchased all
of its outstanding Preferred Stock for its book value of $6,553,000, and
452,856 shares of its Common Stock for $3,633,000, or $8.02 per share, in a
private transaction (the &#147;Block Repurchase&#148;).&#160;
The Company paid for the Block Repurchase with $10,185,000 of
subordinated debt.&#160; Subsequently, a
substantial portion of the subordinated debt was prepaid using the Company&#146;s
line of credit.&#160; In conjunction with the
Block Repurchase, the 2003 Buy Back was cancelled.&#160; In October&nbsp;2004, the Company announced a
plan to repurchase up to $2,000,000 of its Common Stock with no time limit (the
&#147;2005 Buy Back&#148;).&#160; As of August&nbsp;31,
2005, the status of the 2005 Buy Back was as follows:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost per share includes commissions where applicable.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the Company paid a dividend of $.06 per share to
common stockholders, or $240,000&#160; in the
aggregate.&#160; In September&nbsp;2005, the
Company announced its intention to pay quarterly cash dividends, and in October&nbsp;2005,
the Company paid a dividend of $.06 per share to common stockholders, or
$236,000 in the aggregate.&#160; In November&nbsp;2005,
the Company announced a dividend of $.06 per share, or approximately $236,000
in the aggregate, to be paid on approximately December&nbsp;20, 2005 to common
stockholders of record as of December&nbsp;9, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Working Capital; Asset Utilization.&#160; </font></i></b>At fiscal year
end, working capital was $16,251,000 in 2003, $19,294,000 in 2004 and
$19,075,000 in 2005.&#160; The increase in
working capital from 2003 to 2004 was due primarily to increases in accounts
receivable and inventory related to increased sales and reduced current
maturities of long-term debt as a result of financial restructuring, partially
offset by an increase in accounts payable.&#160;
Working capital at August&nbsp;31, 2005 was approximately the same as at
August&nbsp;31, 2004.</p>

fluctuation, and the rates on the revolving line of credit are subject to
reduction as the Company achieves certain financial milestones. See also Note
10 in the &#147;Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements&#148; of the Company in this
Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Summa believes that cash flows from operations and existing credit facilities
will be sufficient to fund working capital requirements, planned capital
expenditures and debt service for the next twelve months.&#160; The Company has a strategy which includes
growth by acquisition.&#160; In the event an
acquisition plan is adopted which requires funds exceeding the availability
described above, an alternate source of funds to accomplish the acquisition
would have to be developed. The Company has 10,000,000 shares of Common Stock
authorized, of which 3,940,041 shares were outstanding at August&nbsp;31, 2005,
and 5,000,000 shares of &#147;blank check&#148; preferred stock authorized, of which none
was outstanding at August&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160;
The Company could issue additional shares of common or preferred stock
or enter into new or revised borrowing arrangements to raise funds.</font></p>

tenant, the Company could become obligated for accelerated lease payments or
