<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a revolving line of credit from its principal bank,
which expires in February&nbsp;2007, with availability of up to $25,000,000,
depending on levels of accounts receivable and inventory.&#160; At August&nbsp;31, 2005, the total capacity
under the revolving line of credit was $19,885,000.&#160; Advances on the revolving line of credit were
$12,343,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2004 and $12,183,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2005,
all classified as long-term.&#160; Depending
on certain financial ratios, interest on the line of credit is at 0.075% to
1.0% below the applicable prime rate or 1.25% to 1.5% above LIBOR, at the
Company&#146;s option, in traunches.&#160; The average
interest rate on the revolving line of credit was 3.1% at August&nbsp;31, 2004
and 5.2% at August&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160; There
is a charge of 0.25% on the unused portion of the line of credit.&#160; The Company has an amortizing, 4.695%, 5-year
bank term loan with a balance of $4,537,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2004 and
$3,546,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160; The
bank loans are secured by substantially all of the Company&#146;s assets, excluding
real estate and equipment related to certain other long-term debt.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s line of credit facility contains certain restrictive
covenants including limitations on borrowing, mergers and acquisitions, paying
dividends and acquiring shares of common stock. Additionally, the Company is
required to meet debt covenants based on certain financial ratios, including an
EBITDA coverage ratio, as defined, of not less than 2.0 to 1.0 at any fiscal
quarter end on or after August&nbsp;31, 2005. The Company was in compliance
with all such bank covenants as of August&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s other long-term debt is primarily comprised of fixed rate
and variable rate loans, secured by related real estate and equipment, with
typical terms of 5 to 10 years.&#160; Average
interest rates on other long-term debt were 4.2% at August&nbsp;31, 2004 and
5.8% at August&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160; The
Company has a subordinated note with a balance of $2,995,000 at August&nbsp;31,
2004 and $686,000 at August&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160;
The interest rate on the subordinated debt at August&nbsp;31, 2005 was
6.5%.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">11.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Preferred
stock and subordinated debt</b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had 5,000 shares of mandatorily redeemable preferred stock,
the holders of which had the right to demand redemption beginning December&nbsp;14,
2004 for $7,025,000, with daily scheduled increases of the redemption
value.&#160; On May&nbsp;3, 2004, the Company
repurchased and retired all of its outstanding preferred stock for $6,553,000,
and 452,852 shares of its common stock at $8.02 per share, by issuance of new,
unsecured, subordinated debt of $10,186,000 with an initial interest rate of
12%.&#160; Subsequently, the Company retired
$9,600,000 of the subordinated debt, with advances from its bank line of
credit.&#160; See Note 10 above.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has adopted a Savings and Retirement Plan.&#160; The plan, which qualifies under Section&nbsp;401(k)
of the Internal Revenue Code, allows employees to defer specified percentages
of their compensation in a tax-deferred trust.&#160;
The Company may elect to make matching contributions and discretionary
contributions, which can be made in cash or the Company&#146;s common stock.&#160; The cost of the Company matching contribution
is partially offset by a reduction in payroll taxes.&#160; Company contributions to the plan totaled
$887,000 in 2003, $846,000 in 2004 and $781,000 in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is subject to legal proceedings and claims arising in the
ordinary course of business.&#160; Although
occasional adverse decisions may occur, the Company believes that the final
disposition of existing matters will not have a material adverse effect on its
financial condition or results of operation.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with a plant acquisition in January&nbsp;2004, the
Company sold approximately 5% of the stock of a subsidiary to the former owner
of the plant. &nbsp;The excess of the purchase price over the stock&#146;s net book
value has been recorded as a gain directly in the statement of stockholders&#146;
equity due to the uncertainty of its realization. Under the terms of the stock
sale agreement, the purchaser has the right to acquire additional shares or,
commencing in January&nbsp;2007, put the shares back to the Company at a price
based upon a prescribed formula.&#160;
Commencing in January&nbsp;2008, the Company has the right to repurchase
the minority interest shares based on a prescribed formula.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for stock options issued to employees and
directors under APB Opinion No.&nbsp;25 and Financial Interpretation No.&nbsp;44.&#160; Under APB 25, if the exercise price of the
stock option equals the market price of the underlying stock on the issuance
date, no compensation expense is recognized.&#160;
Consequently, no compensation expense was recognized under these plans
for fiscal years 2003, 2004 and 2005.&#160;
The Company is required by SFAS No.&nbsp;123 &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based
Compensation&#148; to provide pro forma disclosures under an alternate fair value
method of accounting.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under these Plans, the options are generally issued with exercise
prices equal to the market price of the Company&#146;s stock on the grant date.&#160; Options vest cumulatively over various
periods, at the discretion of the Board of Directors, up to five years from the
grant date, are exercisable in whole or in installments, and expire up to ten
years from the date of grant.&#160; All option
grants during the three year period ended August&nbsp;31, 2005 were pursuant to
Stockholder approved plans.&#160; Options that
are forfeited are again available for grant under the Plans.&#160; All options fully vest immediately prior to a
change in control of the Company, as defined in the stock option plans.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">18.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Acquisitions</b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
January&nbsp;19, 2004, Summa acquired certain assets from the Micro-irrigation
division of R.M. Wade&nbsp;&amp; Co. (&#147;Wade&#148;), including the product brand &#147;Pepco&#148;
and transitional rights to the product brand &#147;Wade Rain&#148;.&#160; Pepco is a brand of products for commercial
landscape irrigation and Wade Rain is a brand of products used in agricultural
irrigation.&#160; The aggregate purchase price
paid for the assets consisted of $1,903,000 in cash, liabilities assumed or
incurred of $97,000 and acquisition costs of $25,000.&#160; The transaction was accounted for using the
purchase method of accounting, and accordingly, the purchase price was
allocated to identifiable tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities
assumed or incurred based upon their fair value at the date of
acquisition.&#160; No goodwill was recorded in
this transaction.&#160; Results of operations
for the period prior to the acquisition were not material and, accordingly, pro
forma results of operations have not been presented.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-20</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">19.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Discontinued
operations</b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2005, the Company&#146;s board of directors approved a plan
to divest the bobbin manufacturing business of Plastron Industries,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Plastron&#148;).&#160; The Company sold certain assets to an
investor group at their book value in September&nbsp;2005 for $300,000 cash and
a $2,280,000 note due in August&nbsp;2006, and leased related equipment and
facilities to the investor group for five years.&#160; Additional assets of Plastron, principally
real estate located in Illinois, will be liquidated as soon as practical.&#160; The Company does not expect to report a
material gain or loss as a result of the transaction.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain assets of Plastron have been reclassified as &#147;assets held for
sale&#148; and certain liabilities of Plastron have been reclassified as &#147;liabilities
held for sale&#148;.&#160; The retained equipment
and facilities remain classified as assets of other ongoing operations.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The financial results of Plastron, which were historically reported as
the Electrical Components operating segment, have been excluded from results of
continuing operations for all periods presented herein and have been presented
as a discontinued operation.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has three reportable segments identified by differences in
products and distribution channels.&#160; The
accounting policies of the segments are the same as those described in the
summary of significant accounting polices.&#160;
The Company&#146;s operations are reported in the following business
segments:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Optical Components.</font></i></b>&#160; In its Optical Components segment, Summa
designs and manufactures plastic prismatic lenses, reflectors and diffusers and
other plastic products, which are used in commercial and industrial lighting
fixtures and other applications.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Material Handling Components.</font></i></b><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&#160; </font></i>In its Material
Handling Components segment, Summa designs and manufactures engineered plastic
components, which form conveyer belts and chains and other plastic products for
use in food processing.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Irrigation Components. </font></i></b>&#160;&#160;In its Irrigation Components segment, Summa
designs and manufactures plastic injection-molded fittings, micro-sprinklers,
emitters, valves, filters and accessories, extruded tubing and other plastic
products for drip irrigation systems used in agriculture, commercial landscape
and other applications.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Formerly, the Company also operated in an Electrical Components segment
which was discontinued in September&nbsp;2005 and is reported as discontinued
operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>
